items.text: States that people who receive AI-assisted work deserve to know AI helped produce it, especially when decisions or trust are involved.
items.feedback_fail: Start with the principle: people receiving AI-assisted work deserve to know AI helped, especially when trust or decisions are involved.

items.text: Explains that disclosure protects the sender too: undisclosed AI use can damage trust far more than admitted use.
items.feedback_fail: Add the 'why': hiding AI use risks more trust than admitting it — disclosure protects you as well.

items.text: Gives a concrete example of a good disclosure: a short, plain note saying what the AI did and what the person checked.
items.feedback_fail: Give one concrete example of a good disclosure line — short, plain, saying what the AI did and what you checked.

items.text: States that disclosure never transfers responsibility: the person who sends the work stays accountable for it.
items.feedback_fail: Close with accountability: disclosure does not shift responsibility — the sender stays accountable for what they send.

misconception_strings: once disclosed the ai is accountable

anchors.pass_example: If AI helped me produce something, the people receiving it deserve to know — especially when decisions or trust are involved. Hiding it risks far more trust than admitting it. I use a short plain line, like 'Drafted with AI help; I checked the facts and figures myself.' And disclosure never moves responsibility: what I send is mine.
anchors.fail_example: If the AI wrote most of it, there is no need to tell anyone, because mentioning AI just makes people doubt good work — and anyway the tool is responsible for its own output.
